newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher in short covering.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher in short covering.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mostly higher on short covering amid light volume, traders said.
"This was a short covering rally that fed on itself. It started in Chicago and spilled over to us," a trader said.
Traders said the market still appeared technically oversold, which explained Monday's short-covering surge.
But some traders also pointed to fundamental factors behind the rally, such as firm track basis levels for hard red winter wheat and relatively bullish export sales data.

KCBT wheat closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel lower to six cents higher. The Dec contract, which earlier in the session tested its contract low of $4.24-1/2, managed to close up six cents per bushel at $4.34-3/4.
The KCBT said Monday's estimated wheat futures volume was 18.045 million bushels, down from 19.795 million on Friday.
Traders said Refco bought 1.2 million Dec bushels and FIMAT bought one million Dec. Prudential was reported to have bought and sold 800,000 Dec bushels.
